subject: Provisioning uplift & rate-band selection for Clearmart renewal
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@clearmart.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-19T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Capacity and rate question ahead of renewal

Marissa —

Thanks for the walkthrough last week. As we map our Q3 projections, the platform spike patterns are shifting: baseline token volume up ~2.4x and peak windows are narrower but higher. We want to land on a renewal that avoids repeated throttling while keeping predictable spend.

Two asks before our internal sign-off:
- Can you share a short recommendation (1 pager) for a commit + burst configuration that limits rate-limited 429s for our current call profile?
- How would billing/proration work if we bump the monthly commit mid-term (start-of-month vs effective date)?

Attaching our Q1 usage export for context.

Happy to hop on a 30-min call if easier — Priya (procurement) will join.

Thanks,
Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Platform, Clearmart
Attachment: clearmart_usage_q1.csv (CSV)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@clearmart.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-19T14:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity and rate question ahead of renewal

Samir —

Appreciate the usage file. I reviewed this with Karthik and Ben; attached is a short options summary (+example numbers) that balances predictability and headroom. TL;DR: two viable paths for renewal:

Option A — Elevated monthly commit + conservative burst pocket
- Monthly commit: increase from 350M tokens to 900M tokens
- Burst pocket: 12% monthly above commit for short windows (enforced per minute)
- Effective for billing: prorated on effective date for partial months
- Good for customers who prefer a single predictable invoice line

Option B — Stepped commit ladder (preferred ops flexibility)
- Commit tiers: 350M baseline -> 650M mid-month -> 900M start of next month
- Soft throttle behavior: gentle shedding above 900M with prioritized fallbacks
- Lower immediate spend, smoother ramp; requires a 45-day runway to implement routing rules

Operational notes in the doc: recommended per-key rate limits (rps-based), cache-priming guidance, and SLA expectations during bridge periods. Karthik, flag any tech concerns below.

If procurement needs the legal SOW and redlineable terms, I can attach a starting SOW and a redline template. Which option do you want pricing for (A or B)?

Next steps suggested:
1) Clearmart picks option or requests hybrid tweaks
2) Ben confirms per-key rate-limit examples for your integration patterns
3) I’ll send SOW + DocuSign for signature and propose effective/proration dates

Thanks — available tomorrow 11:00–12:30 PT for a quick call.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachment: provisioning_options.pdf (PDF)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@clearmart.com>
Date: 2028-06-20T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity and rate question ahead of renewal

Looping in operational detail from the runtime/ops side. Samir — quick notes so you can validate with your platform team: 

- Latency & SLAs: With Option A (single large commit) we can maintain 95th pct latencies inside your current SLA targets for steady-state traffic; brief spikes may see token-latency increase ~12–20ms for 95th pct in the 30–120 second windows.
- Rate-limiting mechanics: we recommend per-API-key sliding window limits: 500 rps per key, soft queueing for 10s, then burst allowance consumption. That maps to ~45K tokens/min per key at average token sizes you sent.
- KV/cache sizing: to avoid cold-start token costs for repeated short bursts, enable prefix caching for common prompt patterns. Ops change required: add an LRU cache flag and attach a stable session id to calls.
- Implementation lead time: Option B’s ladder needs the routing policy + canary rollout (approx 2–3 weeks for config + QA), Option A is doable in 3–5 business days for simple config + billing flags.

Ben — I included per-key rate samples in the attached redlines doc for pricing.

Happy to run a 30-min technical walkthrough with your infra team this week.

—Karthik
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: redlines_clearmart.docx (DOCX)
From: Priya Singh <priya.singh@clearmart.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@clearmart.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-21T08:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity and rate question ahead of renewal

Marissa/Karthik —

Thanks for the clear options. Procurement ran the numbers with finance and we prefer Option B (stepped commit ladder) but with a larger initial mid-month step: start 650M immediately (prorated for June), then automatically step to 900M at the beginning of August. We do want a 10% burst pocket instead of 12%.

Two procurement items before signature:
1) Confirmation that proration will be applied pro-rata by day for the partial month (yes/no).
2) A single invoice per month with a separate billing memo for burst usage (not charged as separate line items if unused).

Also please send the DocuSign for signatures and an expected service activation date (we need to show it to finance).

Priya Singh
Senior Procurement Manager, Clearmart
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Priya Singh <priya.singh@clearmart.com>, Samir Patel <samir@clearmart.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-22T16:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity and rate question ahead of renewal

Priya/Samir —

Great — we can do the hybrid stepped-ladder you described. Confirmations: 
- Proration: yes, we will prorate by day for the initial mid-month uplift (you will only be billed for the days at 650M vs 350M for June).
- Billing presentation: we will issue a single monthly invoice; burst consumption will be aggregated and shown in a billing memo. If burst usage is unused, there is no separate charge.
- Burst pocket adjusted to 10% as requested.

Next steps (action items):
1) I’ve attached the redline-friendly SOW and pricing addendum; please review and comment within 48 hours.
2) DocuSign envelope created for Clearmart legal — link: https://www.docusign.com/envelopes/0A1B2C3D4E5F
3) Proposed activation: provisioning change for mid-month uplift will be scheduled for 2028-06-25 00:00 PT (post-signature), full ladder to 900M scheduled for 2028-08-01 00:00 PT.
4) Karthik will run a deployment checklist and coordinate a 1-hour tech handoff with your infra team on 2028-06-24.

If all good I’ll circulate the final DocuSign and mark the HubSpot deal (link: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/4921).

Thanks — looking forward to getting Clearmart the headroom you need.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: provisioning_options.pdf, redlines_clearmart.docx
